text: COMMERCIAL, STATE-OF-THE-ART, FOSSIL-BASED AMMONIA PRODUCTION 1.5 AMMONIA PROJECTS WITH CARBON CAPTURE While carbon capture and storage (CCS) is not widely adopted in existing U.S. ammonia plants, many planned ammonia projects propose to include CCS. The Air Products Port Arthur SMR plant includes carbon capture via vacuum swing adsorption and is currently operating with two SMR trains as part of the Gulf Coast H network, which uses H for NH . A new SMR plant is 2 2 3 planned for Texas City, Texas, and will be operated by Gulf Coast Ammonia LLC (Business Facilities, 2020). The plant is projected to produce 1.3 MM tonnes/year NH , which is larger 3 than 97 percent of all operating natural gas-based NH plants (Business Facilities, 2020). 3 Multiple new projects plan to use ATR technology with CCS. CF Industries has two planned ammonia plants that include capture in Yazoo City, Mississippi, and Donaldson, Louisiana, targeting startup in 2028. A new plant operated by Nutrien was planned for Geismar, Louisiana, and would have used the Uhde ammonia technology to produce 1.3 MM tonnes/year ammonia with a single train; however, as of 2023, the project was suspended due to high costs and nitrogen fertilizer market volatility (Dill, 2022) (Tullo, 2023). Although the technology is not explored in this report, natural gas partial oxidation (POX) technology can also be used to produce the hydrogen required for an ammonia plant. The Air Products plant in Ascension Parish plans to use POX for ammonia production. New ammonia projects in the United States were announced related to DOE’s H Hub initiative. 2 Ammonia from natural gas will be produced utilizing Haldor Topsoe’s ATR SynCOR technology with up to 99 percent CCS (CNX, 2023). The plant will be located in Mingo County, West Virginia, as part of the ARCH2 H Hub. Ammonia capacity is estimated at 2.16 MM tonnes/year (CNX, 2 2023). Furthermore, KeyState is planning to produce ammonia using Topsoe’s SynCOR technology in Pennsylvania as part of the ARCH2 H Hub (KeyState Energy, 2024). An additional 2 feature of the plant will be electricity generation via excess process steam (KeyState Energy, 2024). 15 COMPARISON OF COMMERCIAL, STATE-OF-THE-ART, FOSSIL-BASED AMMONIA PRODUCTION 2 DESIGN BASIS This section discusses the design basis for the three ammonia cases evaluated in this report. This ensures sound, consistent, and transparent technology assessments and comparisons within and across NETL studies.
